preconditions.description: The number of packages n must be between 1 and 1000.
Each package name must be a string of up to 40 non-whitespace characters.
Each package can have at most 20 dependencies.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'cannot be ordered' if not is_orderable else sorted(order) == order
postconditions.description: If the packages cannot be ordered, output 'cannot be ordered'. Otherwise, output the packages in lexicographically first order.

postconditions.expression: all(package in order for package in package_names)
postconditions.description: All package names must appear in the output order.

postconditions.expression: all(all(dep in order[:order.index(package)] for dep in package_dependencies[package]) for package in package_names)
postconditions.description: Each package must be installed after all its dependencies.

candidate_issues.instruction: Replace the expression to correctly handle the lexicographical order and the 'cannot be ordered' condition.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: For each test case, output the order of package installation that allow them all to be installed after their respective dependencies. If there are multiple possible orderings, then give the ordering that is lexicographically first (using ASCII values for string ordering). If there is some group of packages that are not able to be ordered within the list, output ‘cannot be ordered’ instead of ordering the packages.
